Mood Disorders

Mood disorders — depressive illness, mania, bipolar disorder, suicide risk and nursing care.

🎯 After this chapter you can

  • Describe the symptoms of depression and mania
  • Differentiate depression from normal sadness
  • Assess suicide risk
  • Give nursing care for mood disorders

In simple words

Mood disorders are illnesses in which mood is disturbed for weeks and interferes with life. Depression pulls the person down; mania pushes him up. When both occur, it is bipolar disorder.

Depression — symptoms

  • Low mood, most of the day, nearly every day
  • Loss of interest and pleasure (anhedonia)
  • Sleep changes — early morning waking (typical)
  • Appetite and weight change
  • Fatigue and tiredness
  • Poor concentration; indecisiveness
  • Worthlessness, guilt, helplessness
  • Thoughts of death and suicide
  • Low libido, constipation, psychomotor slowing

Diagnosis: symptoms for over 2 weeks with functional impairment.

Mania — symptoms

  • Elevated, expansive or irritable mood
  • Increased energy with reduced need for sleep
  • Grandiosity and inflated self-esteem
  • Pressure of speech and flight of ideas
  • Overspending and reckless behaviour
  • Distractibility
  • Increased sexual activity
  • Psychotic features in severe mania

Suicide

  • Warning signs: previous attempt, hopelessness, giving away things, sudden calm after despair, sleep loss, alcohol abuse, isolation
  • Nursing: ask directly, remove the means (poison, medicines, weapons), do not leave the patient alone, one-to-one observation, remove ligature points
  • Never promise secrecy — safety over confidentiality
  • Refer and support the family

🔴 Suicide precautions

Remove every means of self-harm. Keep the environment free of medicines, sharp objects, ropes and belts. Maintain continuous observation and never leave the patient alone.

Nursing care

  • Depression: listen, do not say “cheer up”, encourage small activities, monitor sleep, food and medicines; take every threat seriously
  • Mania: low-stimulation environment, firm limits, short sentences, redirect energy, prevent exhaustion and injury; firm but respectful
  • Mania: channel energy into structured activity; never argue
  • Family: educate about the illness, relapse signs and adherence

🔴 Most important for exams

  1. Depression needs low mood or loss of interest for more than 2 weeks.
  2. Early morning waking and diurnal variation (worse in the morning) are typical of depression.
  3. Anhedonia = loss of pleasure in previously enjoyed activities.
  4. Mania shows elated mood, reduced sleep, grandiosity and impulsivity.
  5. Bipolar = episodes of both mania and depression; lithium is the mainstay.
  6. Never promise secrecy about suicidal plans.

⭐ Important for exams

  1. Medicines: SSRIs and TCA antidepressants; mood stabilisers for bipolar.
  2. ECT is considered in severe suicidal depression.
  3. Cognitive therapy is effective for mild to moderate depression.
  4. Postnatal depression and adolescent depression need screening.
  5. Psychotic depression is treated with an antidepressant plus an antipsychotic or ECT.

📌 Memory trick

Depression signs = SIGECAPS: Sleep, Interest, Guilt, Energy, Concentration, Appetite, Psychomotor, Suicidal.

60-second revision

  • Depression: low mood, anhedonia, sleep and energy loss, guilt, suicidal thoughts.
  • Mania: elated or irritable mood, little sleep, grandiosity, overspending.
  • Bipolar: both episodes; lithium and psychotherapy.
  • Suicide risk: ask, remove means, constant observation.
  • Nursing: listen and activate in depression; limit and protect in mania.

Test yourself

The minimum duration for a diagnosis of depression is:

Answer: B. Core symptoms must be present for at least two weeks with functional impairment.

Early morning waking is typical of:

Answer: B. Early morning waking with diurnal variation (worst in the morning) is typical of depression.

Loss of pleasure in usual activities is called:

Answer: B. Anhedonia means loss of interest and pleasure in normally enjoyable activities.

Mood stabiliser of choice in bipolar disorder is:

Answer: B. Lithium is the classic mood stabiliser for bipolar disorder; check therapeutic level regularly.

A patient talks of suicide. The nurse should:

Answer: B. The nurse must take the threat seriously, assess risk, remove means and maintain continuous observation; secrecy cannot be promised.
